descriptions.value: The 1799 constitution placed Bonaparte in the office of First Consul and created a conservative Senate. This republican Consulate preceded the imperial transition in 1804; the same map label should not be read as an unchanged governmental form.

After the Hundred Days, Louis XVIII re-established the Chamber of Peers. The Charter framework gave legislative roles to the monarch and two chambers. The 1815 calendar year includes the interrupted restoration and Napoleon’s return; this curated record begins only with the documented reconstitution in August.

The 1875 constitutional laws established a republican parliamentary framework with two chambers and ministers responsible to them. Parliament moved back from Versailles to Paris in 1879. Presidents and parliamentary institutions are distinct from the rapidly changing ministries.

Defeat and occupation in 1940 produced competing claims to French authority. Pétain’s constitutional acts adjourned the parliamentary chambers, while de Gaulle led Free France. In August 1944 the provisional authorities asserted that republican legality had continued and repudiated the Vichy constitutional acts.

The provisional government restored republican authority, with de Gaulle heading the September 1944 government until January 1946. The later Fourth and Fifth republics had different constitutional frameworks. Presidential terms are retained separately, including Auriol, Coty and de Gaulle; detailed ministry and transition gaps remain unfilled.

Responsibility in Britain passed to a Secretary of State for India, while the Crown appointed the viceroy and governors. Later constitutional reforms changed the institutions within this imperial framework. This arrangement is commonly described as the British Raj. It was an imperial system, rather than an independent national government. The mapped entity should not be read as proof of uniform direct British administration across all of the subcontinent. Princely states had a distinct position, and the geographical dataset’s authority fields provide only a simplified representation. This dossier keeps that distinction visible rather than treating administrative control as an unqualified statement of sovereignty.

The viceroy declared India a belligerent in the Second World War in 1939 without consulting the elected provincial representatives. The Indian National Congress intensified its campaign for independence. British imperial administration therefore faced both the demands of war and opposition to continued colonial rule. New Delhi was the administrative capital. The broader Indian census totals shown separately exclude Burma and should not be read as the population of a single directly administered map polygon. The later partition into India and Pakistan is recorded as a dated transition, not inferred from overlap between map snapshots.
